headline: The war premium is leaking out of crude — Brent -5.2% to 109.81 on Tehran de-escalation talks — and the Fed gets its inflation gift on day one of the FOMC, but the money is still buying utilities and staples, not beta.
summary: The inflation constraint loosened today, and it loosened for the right reason. Brent fell 5.2% to 109.81 as Iran–Saudi de-escalation talks in Tehran bled out the geopolitical premium that had taken it to a six-month high; WTI slipped 0.9% to 100.83. RBOB is now -8.2% on the month at z=-0.88. That lands on a rates complex where the tightening impulse was already decelerating hard into tomorrow's decision: 10y at exactly 5.00% but -17bp on the month with acceleration z=-1.92, 2y 4.68% (-13bp, acc -2.06), 10y real 2.66% (-17bp, acc -1.97), 30y -2bp today. TLT is +3.4% on the month with acceleration +1.37, IEF +1.6% with the highest acceleration in the credit block (+1.70), and MOVE eased to 102.19. The levels are still punitive — the 30-year mortgage is pinned at 7.32%, 94th percentile of the year, and the inflation composite sits at -47 — but the second derivative has turned. Risk regime improved to -19 from -22.

What changed from yesterday is geography. The Brazil accident did not spread but it did not heal: USD/BRL is 5.4088, +7.4% on the week, z=1.23 and still turning up, with Bovespa and EWZ carrying Monday's -13.9% and -19.8% prints. Korea, by contrast, is bouncing — KOSPI +3.1% today (still -20.4% on the month at z=-2.82) with EWY +1.0% — and crucially the won never broke: USD/KRW is -3.0% on the month at the 2nd percentile of its year. The pressure migrated into the majors instead. EURUSD fell 0.6% to 1.1152, the 0th percentile of 52 weeks; DXY +0.3% to 102.22, 94th percentile; USD/CHF 90th percentile; USD/JPY back to 157.68. A slow, broad dollar grind is a more corrosive tightening than one-country blowups, and EEM/SPY is still z=-2.05 at the 13th percentile.

Underneath the index the composition is defensive and accelerating, which is the real tell. XLU is +7.7% on the month with acceleration 2.23, XLP +7.2% with acceleration 2.07, SPLV acceleration 2.39, USMV at the 99th percentile, MCD acceleration 2.37, HD 2.17, WMT +11.4% on the month. Against that, high-beta/low-vol is -14.9% on the month at z=-2.39 with acceleration -2.55, growth/value sits at the 6th percentile of its year, discretionary/staples at the 6th, IWM/SPY at the 20th, and equal-weight/cap-weight rolled over today (-0.4%) despite carrying the highest acceleration on the board at +3.18. The two-day semis bounce — SOXX +2.9%, SMH +2.7%, MU +3.0%, AMD +2.8%, NVDA +2.4% — is a bounce off z=-1.69, not a reversal: SMH is still -10.7% on the month and SMH/SPY is z=-1.79 with acceleration -1.95. Leadership has genuinely moved to software and cyber: IGV/SMH z=2.55 with acceleration 2.11 and +17.7% on the month, CIBR +8.5% on the week at the 97th percentile.

Dispersion is where the money is. LMT ripped 5.1% today, +15.9% on the week and +22.3% on the month at z=2.91 with acceleration 2.97 — 13.1% above its 200-day — while its own sector ITA is -3.1% on the month and BA sits at the 13th percentile; that is an earnings move, not a war trade, and it is extended into a de-escalation headline. Comm services remains the funding short: XLC -1.6% on an up tape, -8.1% on the month, 0th percentile, META acceleration -2.95, NFLX -3.0% and also 0th percentile. The precious-metals unwind deepened — silver -16.7% on the month (z=-1.88), platinum -14.8% (0.5 percentile), gold 4,025 and -6.9%, GDXJ -17.5%, gold/silver +11.9% with acceleration 1.43. The AI-power complex keeps bleeding regardless: REMX -22.4%, NLR -13.9% at the 1st percentile, uranium -16.0%, GRID -9.2%, ETN z=-2.29. Credit is soft but not cracking (HYG/IEF -2.0% on the month, z=-1.5, HYG at the 40th percentile against an S&P at the 90th) and VIX came in 2.8% to 17.87. Growth is not the problem — copper +1.9% with copper/gold at the 100th percentile — the price of risk is.

good.text: The tightening impulse is decelerating into the decision: 10y at 5.00% but -17bp on the month with acceleration z=-1.92, 2y -13bp (acc -2.06), 10y real 2.66% (acc -1.97), MOVE down to 102.19 and TLT +3.4% on the month.
Brent -5.2% to 109.81 as the Middle East risk premium deflates, with RBOB -8.2% on the month at z=-0.88 — the single most helpful input the Fed could get on day one of the meeting.
The growth pulse is fine: copper +1.9% to 6.63, copper/gold +6.3% on the month at the 100th percentile of its year, DBC at the 97th. This is not a demand scare.
Asia is stabilizing where it broke: KOSPI +3.1%, Nikkei +1.7%, EWY +1.0%, and USD/KRW -3.0% on the month at the 2nd percentile — the currency never cracked with the equity.
Volatility is bleeding lower: VIX -2.8% to 17.87 (25th percentile), VIX3M -2.6%, term structure -2.9% and SKEW -6.7% on the week.

New leadership is identifiable, not just defensive: CIBR +8.5% on the week at the 97th percentile, IGV +5.1% on the week, software/semis z=2.55 with acceleration 2.11, XLV relative strength +5.8% on the month and turning up.

bad.text: The dollar is doing the tightening now: DXY 102.22 at the 94th percentile, EURUSD 1.1152 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, USD/CHF at the 90th, and USD/BRL still +7.4% on the week at z=1.23.

Risk appetite keeps narrowing: high-beta/low-vol -14.9% on the month at z=-2.39 with acceleration -2.55, growth/value at the 6th percentile, IWM/SPY at the 20th, and equal-weight/cap-weight rolling over (-0.4% today).

The accelerating bid is defensive, which is bearish information: XLU acceleration 2.23, XLP 2.07, SPLV 2.39, USMV at the 99th percentile, MCD 2.37, HD 2.17. Nobody pays up for staples in a healthy tape.

The hard-asset unwind deepened: silver -16.7% on the month (z=-1.88, 10th percentile), platinum -14.8% at the 0.5 percentile, gold -6.9% to 4,025, GDXJ -17.5%, gold/silver +11.9% with acceleration 1.43.

The AI-power and thematic complex is still in liquidation regardless of the chip bounce: REMX -22.4% on the month, NLR -13.9% at the 1st percentile, uranium -16.0%, GRID -9.2%, COPX -14.9%, ETN z=-2.29.

Credit and housing refuse to confirm the index: HYG/IEF -2.0% on the month at z=-1.50 with HYG at the 40th percentile versus an S&P at the 90th, and the 30-year mortgage stuck at 7.32%, 94th percentile.

trades.name: Long duration into the FOMC
trades.line: Long TLT 81.7 / Dec calls: the impulse is decelerating
trades.expr: Buy TLT outright at 81.68, or Dec 85 calls for convexity; futures alternative is long TY/US into the statement.
trades.thesis: Yield levels are still punitive but every acceleration z-score across the curve is deeply negative (2y -2.06, 5y -1.98, 10y -1.92, 10y real -1.97) and the month's changes are -13 to -18bp. Crude cracking removes the Fed's last excuse to sound hawkish. You are paid on a pause plus a dovish second derivative.
trades.trigger: Brent -5.2% to 109.81 and RBOB -8.2% on the month at z=-0.88 on day one of the meeting; TLT +3.4% on the month with acceleration +1.37, IEF the highest acceleration in the credit block at +1.70, MOVE down to 102.19.
trades.stop: 10y back above 5.15% or TLT below 79.5; also exit if 5y breakevens (2.47%, +13bp on the month, turning up) push through 2.60%.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: leadership has already changed
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long IGV versus short SMH, 1x notional each.
trades.thesis: The ratio has broken out — IGV/SMH +17.7% on the month, +24.1% on 3m, z=2.55 with acceleration 2.11 — yet it is still only at the 38th percentile of its own year, so there is room. Semis are extended on fundamentals and fragile on positioning; software is compounding with cyber (CIBR 97th percentile).
trades.trigger: Today's semi bounce (SMH +2.7%, SOXX +2.9%) gives a better short entry off a 1-month z of -1.45; SMH/SPY is still z=-1.79 with acceleration -1.95 and SMH -10.7% on the month, while IGV is +5.1% on the week with 3m relative strength +18.0%.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below 0.195, or SMH/SPY making a new one-month relative high.

trades.name: Fade the crude-beta extension
trades.line: Short XOP vs SPY: oil cracked, the equity hasn't marked it
trades.expr: Short XOP at 204.86 against equal-notional long SPY; or buy XOP December puts ~10% out of the money.
trades.thesis: Energy equity is priced for a war premium that is actively deflating in Tehran. XOP sits 21.7% above its 200-day at the 100th percentile of its year, +12.9% on the month at z=1.02, XLE 20.6% above its 200-day. This is a mean-reversion of extension, not a structural bear call — XLE's 3m relative strength of +15.6% stays the long-term trend.
trades.trigger: Brent -5.2% today to 109.81 with Brent acceleration -0.88, WTI -0.9%, gasoline -3.2% on the day and -8.2% on the month at z=-0.88, while XOP's 1-month relative strength is still +13.8%.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 115 or WTI closes above 105; XOP making a new high.

trades.name: Defensive acceleration
trades.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB: the bid is in low vol, not beta
trades.expr: Equal-notional long SPLV versus short SPHB; USMV versus ARKK is the higher-octane version.
trades.thesis: The defensive complex is not just up, it is accelerating faster than anything else on the board, while high beta is being systematically liquidated. Until breadth confirms, own the thing the flow is buying.
trades.trigger: SPLV acceleration 2.39, XLU 2.23, XLP 2.07, MCD 2.37, HD 2.17, USMV at the 99th percentile — against SPHB/SPLV -14.9% on the month at z=-2.39 with acceleration -2.55 and still only the 49th percentile of its year, with equal-weight/cap-weight rolling over -0.4% today.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV reclaims 1.92 (back above its 200-day) or VIX trades below 15.

trades.name: Korea mean reversion
trades.line: Long EWY: the equity broke, the won never did
trades.expr: Buy EWY at 152.72; add January calls for the gap-fill. Hedge the beta with a small SPY short if you want it pure.
trades.thesis: A 20% one-month drawdown at z=-2.82 with the currency simultaneously at the strong end of its year is a positioning unwind, not a funding crisis. Taiwan held (+10.8% on 3m, 84th percentile), so this is idiosyncratic and therefore mean-reverting.
trades.trigger: KOSPI +3.1% today with acceleration improving from -2.52; EWY +1.0% and 5.7% below its 200-day after -18.4% on the month at z=-2.21; USD/KRW -3.0% on the month and at the 2nd percentile of 52 weeks.
trades.stop: USD/KRW back above 1,360 or KOSPI closes below 5,300.

trades.name: Short the euro at 52-week lows
trades.line: Short EUR/USD 1.1152 toward 1.09; DXY at 94th pctile
trades.expr: Short EURUSD spot or futures from 1.1152; ETF version is long UUP. Size for a 120-pip stop.
trades.thesis: EUR is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range with no obvious catalyst to reverse it: US 10s at 5.00%, European equity leadership broken (EWI -8.3%, EWP -6.5% on the month), and the move is confirmed as dollar-wide by USD/CHF at the 90th percentile rather than euro-specific.
trades.trigger: EURUSD -0.6% today to 1.1152 (-2.0% on the month, z=-0.94) and DXY +0.3% to 102.22, +1.2% on the month at the 94th percentile; EFA/SPY still at the 10th percentile of its year.
trades.stop: 1.1270 (above last week's range) or DXY back under 101.

trades.name: Health care over communications
trades.line: Long XLV / short XLC: 95th percentile against the 0th
trades.expr: Equal-notional long XLV versus short XLC; express the short leg in META if you want the higher beta.
trades.thesis: One sector has accelerating relative strength with earnings behind it, the other is making new 52-week relative lows with its two largest weights in freefall. This is the cleanest trend pair on the board and it funds itself.
trades.trigger: XLV +5.0% on the month at z=1.08 with acceleration 1.13, relative strength +5.8%/+6.1% and turning up, LLY +8.1% and UNH +9.1% on the month, IHI acceleration 1.76 — versus XLC -1.6% on a +0.7% S&P day, -8.1% on the month at the 0th percentile, META acceleration -2.95 and NFLX -3.0% at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: XLC reclaims its 200-day (currently 7.8% above spot) or META turns positive on acceleration above its 200-day.
